exploration.title: Cell Explorer
exploration.subject: Biology
exploration.summary: Inspect cell structures, then test how molecule type and a specific carrier affect passive membrane transport.
exploration.question: Why can the same concentration difference move oxygen across a membrane but leave glucose blocked?
exploration.explanation: Plant and animal cells share a membrane, nucleus and mitochondria. This photosynthetic plant-cell example also has chloroplasts, a cell wall and a large central vacuole; many plant cells lack chloroplasts. A lipid membrane is selectively permeable. Oxygen can diffuse through its lipid interior, while polar glucose needs a specific transport protein. Facilitated diffusion through that carrier still moves glucose down its concentration gradient without energy input. Equal-size compartments, relative concentration units and fixed one-unit steps make the comparison visible; they are not measurements or elapsed time.

experiments.title: Compare molecules
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Start each trial at outside 12 and inside 4. Keep equal compartment size, cell type, carrier off and one model step fixed; change only the molecule from oxygen to glucose.
experiments.observe: Oxygen changes from 12.0/4.0 to 11.0/5.0, while glucose stays at 12.0/4.0 without its carrier. Explain why a concentration difference drives net movement only when the membrane provides a path.

experiments.title: Add a carrier
experiments.instruction: Predict first. Use glucose at outside 12 and inside 4 in both trials. Keep equal compartment size and one model step fixed; change only whether the specific glucose carrier is present.
experiments.observe: Without the carrier glucose stays at 12.0/4.0; with it glucose changes to 11.0/5.0 while the total stays 16.0 relative units. Explain why a selective path enables facilitated diffusion but does not create or pump glucose.

exploration.misconception: Equal concentration does not mean molecules stop moving; it means opposite movements balance so net transfer is zero. Plant cells also have mitochondria, and their wall lies outside rather than replacing the selectively permeable membrane.
